1.note: דיוזגי is obscure; it probably represents a foreign term for dialogue or disputation, referring to the dialogue form of the book of Job. The rendering is tentative.

2.note: The dictum 'Chronicles was given only to be expounded' is known from Vayikra Rabbah 1 and Ruth Rabbah; the reference to Bereshit Rabbah 61 is kept as given.

3.note: The sense is unclear. It may mean 'with differences among them,' or באחזתם may be the opening word of 1 Chr 9:2 ('in their possessions'). Rendered tentatively.

4.note: The page numbers presumably refer to the Latin edition of Philo that de' Rossi used. The English titles are approximate renderings of his Hebrew descriptions.

5.note: Literally 'in his scroll of secrets'; it is unclear which work of Rav Sherira is meant.

6.note: The phrase is obscure; it is rendered as 'let it be among those who believe it,' i.e., left to whoever accepts it.

7.note: This probably refers to Jacob ben Ḥayyim ibn Adoniyahu, author of the introduction to the second Venice Rabbinic Bible (1524-25). The initial ז' is unexplained, so the name is left as given.

8.note: The Aramaic phrase from b. Berakhot 59a (a necromancer's cry) is left untranslated; its meaning is debated.

9.he: אי מן אולפן ... ואי מן אגדה
9.note: The sense of this citation from Bereshit Rabbah, contrasting a teaching from which one does not retract with an aggadah from which one does, is unclear in this context.
